migration.migration_reason: Preserved paid Language Quality findings were independently re-adjudicated against the current fixed five-component design rubric. Legacy normalized scores were retained only for audit and were not used to derive component levels. The snapshot is bound to exact source evidence and the current validator recomputes scores.

recertifier.provider_model_provenance_claim: No Anthropic/Sonnet call is claimed for these reconstructed judgments.

component_findings.actionability: Recertified level 4 under the current criterion: Messages normally provide enough precise information to correct the issue without requiring unrelated guesswork; suggested fixes count only when semantically reliable. Evidence basis: Type erasure means unsound casts/any bypass static diagnostics entirely, producing later, less specific runtime errors instead of caught compile-time errors. | Some diagnostic messages for deeply nested generic/conditional types become verbose and hard to parse (structural type mismatch dumps). | No built-in exhaustiveness-checking diagnostic beyond manual never assertions in switch statements. | Assessed compile-time and runtime diagnostic quality using tsc static analysis expectations on representative micro/adversarial programs, plus known TypeScript/Node.js runtime error reporting characteristics (stack traces, source maps). | tsc provides structured diagnostics (error code, message, file:line:col, and often a source excerpt) for the type errors intentionally probed by adversarial fixtures such as ADV-01_C.ts/ADV-22 bigint-narrowing conversions. | Deeply recursive adversarial cases (ADV-21_depth1000.ts, ADV-21_depth10000.ts) are designed to trigger runtime RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded, which Node.js reports with a truncated but instrumented stack trace; source maps map back to original .ts lines when enabled. | Because TypeScript type errors are compile-time-only (erased at runtime), certain type violations occurring only through any/unsafe casts or external JS interop surface as opaque runtime TypeErrors rather than the richer compile-time diagnostics. | ts…

metric.diagnostics.limitations: Comparison-language reprojection requires the preserved paid source evidence plus the historical program/workload/toolchain inputs to match the current shard; mismatches remain misses.
metric.diagnostics.selection_rule: Judge built-in compiler/checker/runtime diagnostic design from normal language use; do not count external IDE/debugger maturity.

component_findings.abstraction_reuse: Recertified level 4 under the current criterion: Functions, modules/types and generic/polymorphic abstraction support reusable composition across ordinary programs. Evidence basis: No native pattern matching / exhaustive match expression (must emulate via switch + never-check). | No true nominal typing or built-in immutable value types; numeric model still bifurcated between number and bigint (evidenced by ADV-01_C.ts, ADV-22a/b conversions). | Erased generics at runtime (type information not available for runtime reflection) unlike languages with reified generics. | Inspected TypeScript adversarial and micro program corpora under template/programs/typescript/{adversarial,micro} to assess expressive surface: structural typing, union/intersection types, generics, mapped/conditional types, template literal types, discriminated unions, async/await, optional chaining, bigint, typed arrays. | ADV-01_C.ts exercises bigint to Number to Int32Array numeric-conversion narrowing semantics, showing rich builtin numeric type support and typed-array interop. | ADV-22a/ADV-22b probe bigint literal typing and truncation behavior at compile boundaries. | Micro benchmark suite (mb00-mb11) escalates in complexity (22 bytes to about 5KB) covering common algorithmic idioms (loops, arrays, recursion, closures) implementable concisely due to first-class functions, arrow syntax, destructuring, and structural interfaces. | Adversarial suite ADV-11..ADV-26 covers deep recursion (ADV-21 variants up to depth 10000), showing stack-limit behavior and large-input handling that stresses…
